cards.text: Friend, grab your apron, because this is page one of the whole Bible. No warm-up, no small talk. It opens with God Himself: "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."
Right now the earth is formless and void, with darkness over the surface of the deep. Dark and empty with nothing going on? Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, and I KNOW that look.

cards.question: Over the dark waters of the formless earth, an angel of the LORD is hovering.
Into all that darkness, God speaks for the very first time. What does He call into being?

cards.text: God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. One sentence, friend. My oven takes TWENTY minutes to preheat, and it still beeps at me like I owe it money.

cards.question: Light and darkness are both there now. What does God do with the two of them?

cards.text: God saw that the light was good. Then He gives the light a name. He calls it "day".

cards.question: God has named the light "day". What does He call the darkness?

cards.text: There was evening, and there was morning, and that's the first day. On day two, God says, "Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters."

cards.question: When God makes the expanse, He puts some of the waters beneath it and some of the waters above it.
God gives the expanse between the waters a name. He calls it ___.

cards.text: Evening, morning, and day two is done. On day three, God tells the waters under the sky to gather into one place.

cards.question: God tells the waters under the sky to gather into one place. Why?

answers.text: So the dry land may appear
So the waters can grow deeper
So the light can shine on them

cards.text: God calls the dry land "earth" and the gathered waters "seas", and He saw that it was good. A whole ocean in ONE place, and friend, I could never get the batteries in that drawer to stay in one corner.

cards.question: On day three, God tells the seas to bring forth the plants.
God says each plant and fruit tree will bear fruit with ___ in it, according to its kind.

cards.text: Evening, morning, day three, and the trees are already bearing fruit, just like God said. Friend, by day three of anything I start, I'm face down in a bowl of chocolate chips.
Day four, friend. God says there should be lights in the expanse of the sky to tell the day and the night apart.

cards.question: God says the lights in the sky will tell day and night apart. What else will they do?

answers.text: Mark the seasons and days and years
Warn of the storms coming in
Guide the sailors across the sea

cards.text: God says these lights will shine upon the earth. Then He makes two great lights, a greater one and a lesser one.

cards.question: Of the two great lights God makes, the greater light is made to rule the ___.
On day four, God makes the two great lights and nothing else for the sky.

cards.text: He made the stars as well, ONE short line for every star in the sky, and friend, my little Berry would've wanted a whole chapter. The lesser light rules the night, God saw that it was good, and that's day four.

cards.question: Day five. God says the waters should teem with living creatures, and ___ should fly above the earth.

cards.text: So God created the great sea creatures and every winged bird, and God saw that it was good. GREAT sea creatures, friend? I get nervous when the hand mixer turns on.

cards.question: God blesses the sea creatures and the birds. Then what does He tell them?

answers.text: Stay in the place I made you

cards.text: Evening, morning, and day five is done. The seas and the sky are full of life.

cards.question: On day six, God calls the next living creatures up out of the seas.

cards.text: God says the earth should bring forth livestock, land crawlers and beasts of the earth, and He makes them all according to their kinds. Land crawlers, friend? A crumb rolled across my counter last week and I jumped on top of the OVEN.
Day six isn't over yet. Then God says, "Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness," and He's not done talking.

cards.question: God says He will make man in His image. What will man do over the fish, the birds, the livestock and all the earth?

cards.text: "So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them." Out of everything made so far, these are the only ones made in God's image.

cards.question: God blesses the man and the woman and tells them to be fruitful, multiply and fill the ___.

cards.text: And not just fill it. God tells them to subdue it and rule over the fish, the birds and every creature that crawls, and friend, that's a BIG job description for people who just got here. I got hired to press cookies, and I still need a timer.

cards.question: Then God tells the people what He has given them for food. What is it?
God leaves the beasts and the birds to find food on their own.

cards.text: Every green plant goes to every creature with the breath of life in it, and it was so. Then God takes one more look, and this time He looks at ALL of it.

cards.question: God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was ___ good.

cards.text: Evening, morning, the sixth day, and the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array. Friend, I've had a batch of dough sitting in my fridge for six days, and it is NOT completed.

cards.question: By the seventh day, God has finished the work He had been doing. What does He do on that day?

answers.text: He rests from all His work
He starts a brand new world

cards.question: Then God does something with the seventh day itself. What is it?

answers.text: He blesses it and sanctifies it
He makes it longer than the rest
He gives it a brand new name

cards.text: God blessed that day because on it He rested from all the work of creation He had accomplished. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because trust me, this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Right now the earth is formless and void... Dark and empty with nothing going on? Friend, I lived in a junk drawer...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The Spirit of God hovering over the waters (Genesis 1:2) is never told on any card. Card 2 leaves it out, and this true-or-false card only says that an angel is NOT hovering, so the baker never learns what was. The card is also pure luck, because nothing before it lets the baker reason about who or what is hovering.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote, 'One sentence, friend.' and the oven joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'God saw that the light was good. Then He gives the light a name. He calls it "day".' It also reads flat, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'each plant and fruit tree will bear fruit with ___ in it.' Genesis 1:11-12 separates the two: seed-bearing plants bear seed, and trees bear fruit with seed. The card says plants bear fruit, which the text does not say.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two beats: the stars, the Berry joke, the lesser light ruling the night, God seeing it was good, and the end of day four.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke 'my little Berry would've wanted a whole chapter' depends on the baker knowing that Berry is Papa Dorin's star-shaped kid who watches the sky. Nothing in this lesson sets that up.
findings.question: Can lesson jokes assume bakers already know Papa Dorin's kids by name, or does a mention of one of the kids need a setup earlier in the lesson, the way a callback does?

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the creation line, 'GREAT sea creatures, friend?' and the hand mixer joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Be fruitful and multiply,' is a famous Bible phrase. It stands out next to the plain, made-up wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'The seas and the sky are full of life' stretches the text. Genesis 1:20-23 says the waters teemed and the birds were told to multiply on the earth. It never says the sky is full.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the creation line, 'Land crawlers, friend?' and the crumb joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'And not just fill it.', the subdue-and-rule sentence, and the timer joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'He blesses it and sanctifies it,' uses the Bible word 'sanctifies.' The wrong answers are plain everyday phrases, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now... trust me...') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
